title: dar: doy, da, dan; te lo doy; ustedes

cards.title: dar = to give; doy = I give
cards.body: Doy rhymes with voy. The rest are regular -ar forms.

examples.en: he gives / they give / you give

cards.title: me lo dan = they give it to me
cards.body: Spanish says 'they give me it': the person word first, then lo, both before the changed verb.

cards.title: Te lo doy mañana
cards.body: With mañana as future context, the present works: a very natural Spanish sentence.

examples.en: I'll give it to you tomorrow.

cards.title: Work out who does what to whom
cards.body: Complicated in English, simple in Spanish: you (formal) give = da; to me = me; it = lo. Usted, yo, él, ella can move around for emphasis; that's best picked up in real conversation.

examples.en: Are YOU giving it to me tomorrow?
examples.es: ¿Usted me lo da mañana? / ¿Me lo da usted mañana?

cards.title: ustedes = you all
cards.body: Words ending in a consonant add -es for the plural.

examples.en: Are you guys giving it to us tomorrow?

cards.title: te lo quiero dar
cards.body: Work out the verbs first (quiero dar), then 'it' and 'to you'. Person first: te lo.

examples.en: I want to give it to you.
examples.es: Te lo quiero dar. / Quiero dártelo.

cards.caveat: The attached form 'dártelo' is standard Spanish too; the lesson uses the version in front.

practice.en: I'll give it to you (informal) tomorrow.
Are you (formal) giving it to me tomorrow?
Are you guys giving it to us tomorrow?
I want to give it to you (informal).
